card.name: Bwiti Dance
card.era: Ancient (Babongo origins; Fang syncretic form early 20th c.)
card.tagline: Sacred trance dance of Gabon's iboga religion
card.profile: Bwiti is a spiritual discipline and one of Gabon's officially recognized religions, practised by the forest-dwelling Babongo, Mitsogo and Fang peoples; music and dance are central to its ceremonies (Wikipedia). Practitioners consume the psychoactive root bark of the Tabernanthe iboga plant in initiation rites, rites of passage and healing ceremonies. Dance, chanting and ritual music - drums, shakers, and the ngombi (sacred harp) or musical bow - accompany all-night ceremonies through which participants reach trance and spiritual connection with ancestors. The N'ganga (ritual leader) and participants typically wear red, black and white cloth, raffia skirts and faces painted with white kaolin (Wikipedia; Kanaga Africa Tours).
card.insight: This is a sacred, religious context, not entertainment: the dance is inseparable from the iboga sacrament and ancestor veneration, and Bwiti is one of Gabon's three official religions (Wikipedia). The tradition is largely oral and many rites are deliberately kept secret.
